fact: Agence Ecofin says Mauritania has been connected to the ACE cable since 2011 and still depends heavily on it, with no fully operational alternative, so ACE outages disrupt internet nationwide; ACE is the single route in service.
The EIB press release says Mauritania connected to the Africa Coast to Europe (ACE) submarine cable in 2010 (other sources say 2011), and that a contract for a second cable was awarded to Ellalink.

EllaLink says it has built a new neutral cable landing station in Nouadhibou that lets Mauritania's national operators access the infrastructure via two diverse routes (landing marked 4 May 2026; the document does not say the branch is yet in service).
DatacenterDynamics reports that only one subsea cable currently lands in Mauritania, the ACE system at Nouakchott, in which International Mauritania Telecom is the Mauritanian participant.
The ACE consortium says the ACE cable was put into service on 15 December 2012 and lists Nouakchott as one of its landing stations, the first international submarine cable to land in Mauritania.
